headline: P&G plans to cut manufacturing and logistics workforce by up to 30% by 2030
summary: Procter & Gamble plans to cut its manufacturing and logistics workforce by up to 30% by 2030 as part of a broader $10 billion cost-saving initiative. Facing rising commodity expenses, inflation, and subdued demand, the consumer goods giant intends to heavily expand automation across its supply chain network. The move follows earlier corporate job cuts after P&G recorded its slowest annual earnings growth since 2016.

headline: Cisco cuts less than 1% of workforce in latest layoff round
summary: Cisco implemented a targeted round of layoffs in November impacting less than 1% of its global workforce as part of an ongoing realignment toward high-demand areas like artificial intelligence. The move follows larger reductions earlier in the year, contributing to a broader headcount decline of nearly 9% between 2024 and 2026. Management expects the operational efficiency gains to boost revenue per employee by approximately 19% while driving incremental growth.

headline: MP scraps two-child rule for government employees
summary: The Madhya Pradesh state government has repealed its 25-year-old two-child restriction for public sector employees and job applicants, citing declining fertility rates across the country. Under the amended civil service rules, individuals with more than two children are now eligible for government jobs, and all ongoing disciplinary actions related to the rule are terminated with immediate effect. However, past cases where final penalties have already been imposed will not be reopened.

headline: Karnataka GCCs employ 43% of India’s AI/ML workforce
summary: Karnataka hosts 43% of India's GCC-based AI/ML workforce and accounts for nearly half of the country's AI/ML centers of excellence, reinforcing its role as a premier technology hub. Bengaluru leads this growth by driving 44% of senior AI leadership postings within these capability centers. Additionally, GCCs in the state are investing above the national average in dedicated AI training and capability development.

headline: Chitrupa Kapoor joins thyssenkrupp Automotive as head-people & culture – India
summary: Chitrupa Kapoor has been appointed as Head of People & Culture – India for thyssenkrupp Automotive’s Bilstein Motion Solutions division. Bringing over 18 years of human resources experience, she previously served as senior HR business partner at Bitwise and held roles at Tata Consultancy Services and Symbiosis. In her new role, Kapoor will lead talent priorities, leadership development, and workforce strategies to align with the company's growth agenda in India.

headline: Maha’s new wage rules put employee rights and fair pay in focus
summary: The Maharashtra government has notified the Maharashtra Wage Rules, 2026, establishing an updated framework for working hours, overtime, and payroll compliance under the national Code on Wages. The new regulations cap work weeks at 48 hours, limit salary deductions to 50%, and redefine wage components to accurately calculate statutory benefits like gratuity. Additionally, organizations must now maintain employee and payroll records for five years while ensuring enhanced wage transparency and dispute resolution mechanisms.

headline: Rising Star: Mugdha Mahambrey on why HR leaders should be capable of running businesses
summary: Mugdha Mahambrey, Head of People & Culture at Chalet Hotels, advocates for treating human resources as a core business function capable of preparing executives for general management and CEO roles. She emphasizes evaluating HR initiatives through a blend of human impact and tangible business metrics, such as productivity and internal leadership pipelines. Pointing to cross-functional movements in the hospitality sector, Mahambrey argues that business leadership and people management must deeply inform one another.

headline: The career mistakes that don’t look like mistakes
summary: Three HR leaders outline subtle career mistakes that initially seem like sound decisions, such as rushing tasks for quick completion, chasing prestigious employer brands over actual learning, and passively following instructions without question. They emphasize that long-term success requires thoroughness, foundational skill building early in one's career, and exercising independent professional judgment.

headline: How employee ownership created thousands of millionaires at Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's recent initial public offering generated unprecedented wealth for its workforce, with nearly 96 percent of its 5,300 employees holding equity worth over $1 million. The company's equity-centric compensation strategy drove exceptionally low attrition and rewarded early tenure over high seniority. Departing from conventional IPO practices, Anthropic also permitted staff to immediately sell a portion of their shares upon listing.

headline: Baskaran Balasubramanian is now executive director-HR technologies, Wells Fargo
summary: Wells Fargo has appointed Baskaran Balasubramanian as Executive Director of HR Technologies following a six-year tenure at Deutsche Bank. With extensive leadership experience across tech and financial firms including Oracle and ADP, he will lead digital platform initiatives for workforce management. His appointment highlights the financial sector's growing focus on integrating deep technology expertise into strategic HR operations.

headline: Nvidia advances employee pay hikes and equity awards
summary: Nvidia has advanced its planned employee salary increases and equity awards to December following the departure of founder and long-time CEO Jensen Huang. Interim CEO Colette Kress announced the accelerated timeline during an all-hands meeting aimed at reassuring staff and retaining talent amidst the leadership change. Despite internal employee appeals for Huang's return, Nvidia's board reiterated that it will not reverse its decision as the search for a permanent successor continues.

headline: Radisson recommends 58 Saudi candidates for jobs, trains 33 employees abroad
summary: Radisson Hotel Group has recommended 58 Saudi hospitality candidates for recruitment and selected 33 local employees for international training placements across Europe. The talent development initiatives support the company's strategy to double its Saudi Arabia portfolio from 50 to 100 properties by 2030. Key partnerships with HTMi Saudi Arabia and the Ministry of Tourism helped facilitate the recruitment and global placement programs.

headline: Nitasha Rama Ghai joins Everise as VP-HR
summary: Nitasha Rama Ghai has joined Everise as Vice President of Human Resources, bringing over 18 years of experience in HR leadership and organizational development. Prior to this role, she provided independent HR advisory services and spent over 18 years holding senior HR positions at Samsung Electronics. Her background spans talent management, strategic workforce planning, employee engagement, and organizational change.

headline: Arundhuti G takes charge of HR at Fitsol
summary: Fitsol has appointed Arundhuti G as its new Head of Human Resources, bringing 16 years of experience in talent acquisition, employee engagement, and organizational development. She previously held senior HR positions at organizations including Prozo, the All India Football Federation, RIVIGO, and Citi India. She holds an MBA from NMIMS and brings expertise in scaling HR charters across diverse business sectors.

headline: Omnicom Media India integrates Interactive Avenues into wider network
summary: Omnicom Media India is integrating digital agency Interactive Avenues into its broader organizational structure to streamline operations and strengthen client offerings. Under the restructuring, Interactive Avenues' core practices and client accounts will primarily move to Initiative India and Lodestar UM. Alongside the transition, Initiative India announced leadership updates, elevating Aparna Tadikonda and Priya Iyer to COOs following the departure of CEO Vaishali Verma.
